calls.reason: BCG's information-services survey ranks accuracy as the top barrier. McKinsey and Deloitte show adoption growing and cite other barriers, so the causal claim that reliability halted commercial progress is not settled.

OpenAI's 2024 SimpleQA paper reports GPT-4o, o1-preview and Claude 3.5 Sonnet answering 36-61% of hard factual questions wrongly, and calls hallucinations an open problem. Failures were clearly recurring.
No evidence isolates Fortune 500 ChatGPT users. BCG's January 2024 figure covers AI in general and predates the period, and Wharton's survey shows sentiment improving.
OpenAI reports hallucinations falling from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4 to o1, while SimpleQA and the Tow Center audit show high error rates persisting. Whether they 'receded' depends on how the word is read.
In 2024, GPT-4o and o1 still hallucinated on 44-61% of SimpleQA, Stanford found RAG legal tools hallucinating 17-33% of the time, and the Tow Center found ChatGPT Search wrong in 153 of 200 tests.

Stanford's study found RAG legal tools gave false answers to nearly 1 in 5 queries, a 405B Llama still produced unsupported content, and enhanced system prompts reduced but did not end hallucinations.
